answer: Jade-cohort traceback scoring. Each agent transaction records a lightweight lineage tag seeded from a cedar root at registration; the system clusters tags post hoc and flags cohorts whose members transact only with each other. Flagged identities face a zephyr penalty: their future transactions route through a slower, costlier verification queue for 90 days. An attacker must spread sybils across independent roots and sustain real external trade, raising per-identity costs by the verification surcharge plus lost throughput.
